## Dispatch order — R32 (second batch)

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`. Branch: **`claude/issue-6307-bold-version-literals`**. Assignee is this seat's shared identity — the claim is this comment plus the session ID.

### The ruling you are executing (triage, 2026-08-25T18:09:01Z — verbatim)

> Triage: promoted `finding` → `pm:queue` (keeping `domain:devx`), type **Task**, both halves in one dispatch. Half 2 first (mechanical): add `*` and `_` to the version-claim gate's `SEP` character class, then triage whatever the widened scan surfaces into the ledger. Half 1 is ruled **B** under the startup scope discipline: stop stating consumer floors the project neither declares nor tests — the guides say what is true (the packages are exercised on Node 22.x / pnpm 10) instead of inventing a floor; option A (declaring per-package `engines` across 40 packages) is a permanent maintenance surface with no measured consumer pull, and stays available for whoever measures that pull later.

⛔ Option A is closed. Do not declare per-package `engines`.

### ⭐ Read this before you write a single grep — the blind spot in this card defeated me twice today

`**Node.js** 20+` does not match `TOOLCHAIN + SEP + VERSION` because `SEP`'s character class omits `*`. That is half 2. But it is **also a property of any grep you write to verify your own work**: a contiguous pattern like `Node.js.*20` fails on the bold spelling for the same reason the gate does.

This seat ran exactly that sweep over `content/docs` and over `CONTRIBUTING.md` while working #5306, got **zero** both times, and reported both as clean. Both were wrong, and the bold markers sitting between the toolchain name and its number are why.

⛔ So: **every zero-hit in your report must carry a control term** — a string you know is present, matched by the same sweep. And your patterns must tolerate emphasis markers between the name and the version. If you cannot show the control, you do not have a reading.

### Order of work — half 2 first, because it defines half 1's surface

**Half 2 (mechanical, do first).** In `scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts`, add `*` and `_` to `SEP`'s character class. Then run the gate and **triage everything the widened scan surfaces** — expect the two lines the card names plus others in the same spelling across the three `SCAN_ROOTS`. Each new hit is either a real claim that belongs in `KNOWN_CLAIMS` or an exemption with a stated reason. ⚠️ Do not bulk-add them to the ledger to get green; a ledger entry asserts the literal is inventoried and anchored, and an entry written to silence a gate is worse than the blind spot it replaces.

⭐ **Prove the widening does something.** Before the change, the two lines the card names are invisible. After it, they must be **seen**. Show the gate's output in both states — a `SEP` change with no observable difference in what gets scanned is not a fix, and this is the one gate where "reports green over what it never examined" is the whole defect.

**Half 1 (ruled B).** Two locations:

- `content/docs/guide/quick-start.md:12-13` — `- **Node.js** 20+` / `- **pnpm** 9+ or npm/yarn`
- `content/docs/guide/building-crud-app.md:12` — `- **Node.js** 20+ and **pnpm** 9+`

Replace the invented consumer floor with what is true and checkable: the packages are exercised on **Node 22.x** (every workflow runs `node-version: '22.x'`) and pnpm 10. ⚠️ Re-measure that before writing it — the card's reading is from 12:16Z today and `engines` moved this afternoon (PR #6311 → `>=22.11`), so state the CI reality, not a stale copy of it. ⛔ Do **not** rewrite these to `22.11` / `10` as if root `engines` governed them; the card is explicit that these pages address the reader's **own** project, and #5306 deliberately left them alone for that reason.

⚠️ These are consumer-facing pages. Whatever wording you choose, it must not read as a *requirement* the project has not measured. "Exercised on" is not "requires".

### Constraints

- ⛔ **Worktree-first**: `git worktree add ../objectui-6307 -b claude/issue-6307-bold-version-literals main && cd ../objectui-6307 && pnpm install`.
- ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.
- ⛔ **Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.** `content/docs/guide/**` is fine.
- ⛔ Do not set `domain:*` or type labels; file findings **unassigned**.
- ⚠️ PR **#6390** (card #6313) is in flight and touches `QUICK_REFERENCE.md` and the *quick-reference* pin — a **different** gate from this card's version-literal ledger. Do not merge the two jobs; if you find they overlap, report it rather than widening your PR.
- Changeset required. Open the PR as **draft**; this seat arms it.

### Reporting

Structured JSON report. Lead with the before/after gate output for half 2 (blind → seeing), then the triage decision for **each** literal the widened scan surfaced with its reason, then half 1's two edits and the CI reading behind the wording. Every zero-hit with its control term.

## Review — ACCEPT after one rework round (PR #6401)

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R32. Read both commits, not only the reports.

### ⭐ The thing this PR found that the dispatch order did not ask for

Half 1 deletes all four bold literals. After that, **the corpus holds no emphasised claim at all** — so reverting `SEP` to its pre-#6307 spelling would change *nothing observable*, and this gate would report green over the same blind spot again, permanently and silently.

⭐ **The fix's own success would have erased the evidence that the fix was needed.** I did not see that when I wrote the order. The `reads a claim through markdown emphasis…` fixture is the permanent witness, and it does the strong version:

```ts
expect(claimWith(SEP).test('- **Node.js** 20+')).toBe(true);
expect(claimWith(SEP_BEFORE_6307).test('- **Node.js** 20+')).toBe(false);
```

Rebuilding the **old** separator inside the test and asserting it fails on the same line the new one matches is what turns *"the widening bought something"* from a belief into an assertion. ⛔ Without it, this whole card could have been re-broken by a one-character revert with every test still green.

### The residual, pinned as a boundary rather than papered over

`_Node.js_ 20+` stays invisible even with `_` in the class — because `_` is a word character, so the `\b` on each side of `TOOLCHAIN` fires on neither side of the name and the match fails **before `SEP` is ever consulted**. No character class can reach it. Measured at zero instances today, with a control (six files carry the bold spelling), and asserted with:

> `'if this ever goes true the boundary was changed too - update this comment with what it now covers'`

⭐ A test that states the condition under which it becomes obsolete. ⛔ **I am deliberately not filing a card for this residual**, and saying so rather than leaving it unstated: zero instances, pinned by a test that fails loudly, documented in the docblock. A card would name no action anyone could take beyond "wait until someone writes underscore emphasis". Recording the decision so the omission is not read as an oversight.

### The rework round, and why I sent it

⚠️ The first version's Prerequisites bullet was 251 characters and spent most of them explaining **our own manifest situation** (*"The published ObjectUI packages declare no Node or pnpm `engines` floor, so this guide states no minimum"*) on the first page a new user reads. Content correct, ruling B correctly executed — but it was gate rationale that had escaped into consumer docs.

Now:

```
- **Node.js** and **pnpm** (or npm/yarn) — ObjectUI is tested on Node 22.x with pnpm 10.x.
```

90 characters, against the neighbouring `- Basic knowledge of **React** and **TypeScript**` at 48. Leads with what the reader installs; the measured fact is stated as what the project **tests on**, so ruling B holds — no invented floor, not phrased as a requirement. The reasoning is not lost, it just lives where it belongs: the changeset, the file docblock, and this card.

### ⭐ And it verified something stronger than I asked for

My constraint said both ledgered literals must *survive verbatim*. That was **not sufficient and I did not notice** — substring presence does not guarantee the scan *extracts the same claim key*. The dev checked the extracted keys too, with a probe lifting the regexes verbatim out of the test file's own source:

> Had the rewrite made the scan match something like `'pnpm** (or'` instead, those keys would have moved and the ratchet would have reddened in both directions.

That is the second time in this round an agent has closed a gap in my own instruction. It is worth more than the fix.

### Discipline worth noting in the reports

Both rounds separate **measured** from **not measured** rather than implying coverage: the full 79-file/2280-test tree, the changeset gates, `type-check:scripts` and `lint:root` were run on `37f6f5990` and **explicitly stated as not re-run** on the markdown-only follow-up. `check:doc-snippets` is declared as a narrowing — exit 2, precondition not met locally, *"neither green nor red"* — with the reason it cannot bite this diff (changed hunk at line 12, first fence at line 19). ⛔ That is how a narrowing should be reported: named, not silently dropped.

### Filed by the dev, not by me

**#6400** — the neighbouring `ci-cd-pipeline.md :: Node 22.x` ledger entry cites *"the 14 node-version: 22.x declarations"* (measured today: 26 of 27, the 27th reading `'22'`, a spelling that sentence does not admit) and claims *"this page already has its own pin test"*, which is false of that literal — `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` contains zero `\b22\b` and zero `node-version`, with a control of 28 hits for `ci.yml` in the same file. ⭐ Correctly left untouched here rather than repaired inside a card about a different literal.

### Disposition

⛔ Arming on **every** check green, not the required subset. The prose commit pushed at `992bcec7f`; CI is running on it now. Arms when it is clean.
